notes.decision: Translated 'transgressor / transgressing word' on the basis of the recurring opposition with ⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sin' (line 15) and the parallel construction ⲣⲉⲣⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sinner' in the corpus. The verb ⲱⲱⲃⲉ characterizes a word/act that 'harms the cross of light' (l.6) and produces demons (l.16). Likely Lycopolitan reflex of a verb of transgression/blame — possibly cognate with ⲱⲡ in the sense 'be charged/accused' or with ⲟⲩⲱⲃⲉ 'oppose.' Confidence moderate.

Tentatively rendered 'the foremost matter' analyzing as ⲡⲱⲣⲡ̄ (= ϣⲟⲣⲡ 'first') + ϩⲁⲧⲉ (cf. ϩⲏ 'front, before'). Alternative readings include 'previously' or 'matter mentioned before.' Functions as a discourse-marker linking back to a prior topic. Confidence low.

notes.decision: Rendered 'the word of the (evil) eye with that-of-wrath and that-of-gall.' ⲥⲉⲭⲉ ⲛⲃⲁⲗ literally 'word of eye' = malicious/envious utterance (cf. evil eye idiom). ⲡⲁⲧⲃⲗⲁⲕⲉ analyzed as ⲡⲁ-(ⲧ-)ⲃⲗⲁⲕⲉ 'the one of wrath' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲃⲗ̄ⲕⲉ 'wrath'); ⲡⲁⲧⲭⲟⲗⲏ 'the one of gall' (Greek χολή). Three-fold catalogue of the venomous-speech vices.

Rendered 'malice indeed.' ⲕⲁⲕⲁϩ likely a Lycopolitan reduplicated form related to ⲕⲱϩ 'envy, jealousy' or to ⲕⲁⲕⲓⲁ 'evil.' ⲙⲙⲉⲧⲉ taken as adverbial 'in truth, indeed' (cf. Sah ⲛⲁⲙⲉ). Alternative reading: ⲕⲁⲕⲁϩ 'discord' + ⲙⲙⲉⲧⲉ 'agreement' = 'malicious agreement.' Confidence low.

Rendered 'shall plot against' analyzing as future ⲛⲁ- + verb ⲥⲁⲣϥ̄ (possibly Lyc. for ⲥⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'ruin, demolish' or ⲥⲱⲣ 'spread/scatter' with 3sg.m suffix). The construction ⲥⲁⲣϥ ⲥⲁ ⲡⲉϥⲥⲁⲛ 'against his brother' fits a hostile-speech action consistent with the surrounding catalogue of accusatorial sins. Alternative: 'shall slander.' Confidence low.

Rendered 'wise physician.' ⲥⲉⲓ̈ⲛⲉ = Lyc. for ⲥⲁⲉⲓⲛ 'physician.' The medical-soteriological simile structures the closing portion: the righteous teacher's word is to the soul what the wise physician's surgical-pharmacological treatment (cutting, cleansing, applying corrosive medicine, burning, piercing) is to the body — apparent harm that effects healing. Standard Manichaean trope.

Rendered 'the iron' (already in glossary). Here used in surgical-metaphorical sense: 'burn her in the iron and pierce her' = cauterizing iron applied to the wounded soul/matter. Direct correspondential continuity with the bitter-tree / iron-body register of earlier kephalaia: the iron now becomes the redemptive instrument when wielded by the wise physician (= righteous apostle).
